new_statements.translation: [p. 113] Ntumbidi has a fairly simple tonal system divided between two level tones and two contour tones: High (H), Low (B), Rising (Mt) and Falling (Dt). [p. 115] Tonally, Ntumbidi shows two tonemes, /H/ and /L/, written with acute and grave accents. Tones have a distinctive function in this variety. However, the author [Mokrani] notes two further facts: an extra-high tone resulting from a sequence of three high tones, the third realised higher than the first two, e.g. [dèfúpókwɛ́↑] 'ash'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Ntumbidi is described purely as a two-tone (H/L) Bantu language with derived rising, falling and extra-high realisations; the description contains no statement locating a word stress or accent. The only accent-related remark in the thesis is comparative and group-wide (p. 238): across B20 the H/L contrast survives mainly on the first stem syllable while the stem-final syllable is regularly Low, which the author reads as an incipient, incomplete drift toward an accentual system — not a synchronic stress rule for Ntumbidi.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress; tonally, an extra-high realisation on the third of three successive H tones is noted.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical/stem tone on citation forms (noun and verb stems, T1/T2 = first/second stem syllable); no phrase-level prosody discussed. The Ntumbidi facts are reported second-hand from Mokrani 2016 (variety not specified there beyond 'ńtùmbìdí'); Koumbi Mabiti did no Ntumbidi fieldwork.
new_statements.identity_note: Koumbi Mabiti (2025: 111) treats ńtùmbìdí as B22d and notes it is variously confused with a Kele (B22a) dialect and with Metombolo (B205); Glottolog's Tombidi [tomb1246] has no ISO code. Two described varieties exist: Rébé (southern Ngounié; Bingoumou 2005/2008, and apparently Mokrani 2016's data point) and Lambaréné / 'Akele des Lacs' = Muntumbudie (Hombert et al. 2009; Mouyissi Mbadinga 2023). The quoted tone statement is Mokrani's analysis as summarised by Koumbi Mabiti; which village Mokrani recorded is not stated in the summary.

sources.note: Section I.2.3.4 Ńtùmbìdí (B22d), printed pp. 111-115 (data explicitly taken from Mokrani 2016): tone system of two level tones H and B plus rising and falling contours (p. 113); two distinctive tonemes /H/ and /B/, plus an extra-high realisation after H-H (p. 115). No statement about word stress/accent for Ntumbidi; the word 'accent' never occurs in the Ntumbidi section.
